thread.title: Dropbox Shares Extend IPO Gains as File-Sharing App Defies Tech Sector Gloom

author: thestreet.com
title: Dropbox Shares Extend IPO Gains as File-Sharing App Defies Tech Sector Gloom
text:
Dropbox Inc. ( DBX ) shares were marked higher again Monday, following the biggest trading-debut jump since the Snap Inc. ( SNAP ) IPO last week, as investors continue to pour cash into file and personal data storage company
Dropbox surged more than 35% Friday, its first day of public trading after raising just over $756 billion in a March 22 IPO that priced the group at $21 a share. Dropbox traded as high as $31.60 each during the session before closing at $28.48 each, a move that values the San Francisco-based company at $11.6 billion.
"For us, what we are excited about is just the massive opportunity we have to scale the business," Dropbox COO Dennis Woodside told TheStreet in an exclusive interview Friday . "We have 500 million registered users around the world, those users have brought us into millions of businesses and we really solve a problem that many businesses and teams have, which is how do you collaborate around my most important content."
"We are excited to welcome @Dropbox to our family of visionaries as they continue to grow, innovate and reimagine the way work gets done." - Nasdaq CEO @AdenaTFriedman
Please like and retweet to help them celebrate their IPO day! #DBX pic.twitter.com/8POdEANlZy
— Nasdaq (@Nasdaq) March 23, 2018 Dropbox shares were marked 4.4% higher in pre-market trading in New York Monday, indicating an opening bell price of $29.74 each and a 41.14% gain from their original IPO price.
The listing was a rare bright spot for the tech sector last week, which slumped 7.9% over a five-day run dominated by news of a data scandal at Facebook Inc. ( FB ) that hived more than $50 billion in value from the world's biggest tech company and ignited calls from both sides of the Atlantic for tighter regulation on companies that use and profit from data collected from their users.
Action Alerts Plus holding Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) CEO Tim Cook told the China Development Forum in Beijing this weekend that "some large profound change is needed" in order to restore public trust in the way that personal data is collected and used by the tech industry, a view echoed by IBM Corp CEO ( IBM ) Virginia Rometty, who called for a new era in which "ownership of the data does belong to the creator". The moves follow revelations that a controversial political consultancy, Cambridge Analytica, improperly obtained user data from Facebook that it may have used to help sway the 2016 elections in favor of President Donald Trump.
"I'm personally not a big fan of regulation because sometimes regulation can have unexpected consequences to it," Cook told the audience in Beijing. "However I think this certain situation is so dire, and has become so large, that probably some well-crafted regulation is necessary."
Dropbox's stunning Friday performance, however, may ease some of those concerns and pave the way for a smooth opening bell debut for Spotify when the music sharing app starts trading on April 3.

As TheStreet's Eric Jhonsa wrote earlier this month, Spotify is taking the unusual IPO path of pursuing a direct listing in which it will not raise new capital nor use underwriters to help set and support the initial trading price.
"Some impressive user engagement figures were shared," at its March 15 investor day. "44% of Spotify's 159 million monthly active users (MAUs) use the service daily, and average daily usage clocks in at 49 minutes. That's nearly on par with the 50-plus minutes of average daily usage Facebook has reported for its core service, Messenger and Instagram. For Spotify's 71 million paid users, the figure is above 80 minutes."
